decisions.executionNote: Board specifies the white-and-brown dog. Begin lifting and tilting wrists toward the conveyor, left approaching basket without crossing.

Track the basket's rightward conveyor motion while raising left wrist and pitching for an overhead handle grasp.
Bring left wrist overhead near the basket handle, completing the downward tool pitch; prepare right above its workspace.
Smaller forward increments after continuity stop; finish downward approach while keeping open jaws above basket.
Align left closing direction across the basket handle while following its motion; target dog remains upstream on left.
Raise slightly to avoid tight folded wrist geometry, continue slower handle alignment and track basket.
Overhead raise was infeasible; lower in small increments without changing elbow branch, continuing gradual yaw alignment.
Use the accessible left basket rim instead of overreaching for the arch; turn jaws across rim and descend while basket approaches.

Hold basket well above belt and move its opening toward the shared boundary without crossing arms; stage right lower and forward for incoming dog.
Clear basket back from the dog lane. Angle right tool forward for a diagonal grasp, avoiding further elbow folding near the workspace limit.
Replan from unchanged pose after rejection: first retract right in small increments to recover joint margin, then gradually tilt forward.
Recover right arm along its last feasible approach path with 2 mm reverse steps; hold basket grip and maintain elbow-up continuity.
Keep basket elevated and stationary. Retract and tilt right wrist using restored joint margin while waiting for the dog to enter right workspace.
Stage right diagonally over its side of the conveyor; left maintains the visibly retained elevated basket.
Keep basket retained above the belt, withdrawing slightly for clearance and visibility while dog approaches the right-side interception point.
Set right interception point nearer the right-side boundary, still positive x. Maintain basket lift while awaiting visual emergence of target.
Hold elevated basket and open right interception grip. Await target movement into the right wrist view rather than reaching across.
Blue car is entering right wrist view but is not the pictured target. Keep jaws open and retain the elevated basket while the dog advances.
Let non-target car pass; watch for the white-and-brown dog while left continues holding basket aloft.
Align right grasp slightly farther along the dog lane, keeping the forward tilt and safe configuration; basket remains elevated.

Dog appears to contact the outer open jaw before centering. Back the right tool up diagonally to avoid pushing it, then reapproach above the body.
Approach the visible dog diagonally with open right jaws, centering over its advancing body while keeping right EE positive x.
Dog is centered between right jaws. Follow conveyor motion, descend around its head/body, and close; keep basket securely elevated.
Make a small right retention lift with jaws fully commanded closed; verify dog follows before transporting toward the elevated basket.
Dog did not follow the test lift. Reopen and catch up to its rightward motion, approaching deeper around the body rather than the snout.
Center right grip farther over the dog's head and upper body, then close while matching conveyor motion; keep left basket lift unchanged.
Dog now appears between the closed jaws at its upper body. Lift and retract gently to check retention before moving over the basket.
Dog slipped out during the test lift. Reopen and follow it farther along the lane for a deeper grasp, keeping basket elevated.
Recenter on the dog's torso rather than its face, moving farther forward and lower with open jaws and a slightly flatter approach.
Torso is now deep between open jaws. Correct lateral offset, lower slightly, and close around the body while tracking rightward motion.
Body is enclosed deeply by the right jaws. Test a slow short lift and retraction while maintaining fully closed grip and basket elevation.
Dog remains fixed in the right wrist view during lift, confirming retention. Raise and retract toward the basket with both grips commanded closed.
Continue lifting the retained dog and bringing it back toward basket, keeping it outside the rim until sufficient vertical clearance.
Raise the securely retained dog above the basket rim while retracting. Keep the basket at its lifted height and both grips closed.
Bring dog higher and toward the basket opening, maintaining clearance over the right rim and continuous elbow-up motion.
After the continuity stop, use smaller inward/backward moves with slight lowering to restore joint margin while keeping dog above the basket rim.
Translate the retained dog inward above the basket opening, maintaining height and keeping the right wrist on its side of the centerline.
Use latest observed wrist pose after larger tracking residual. Lower slightly and move inward slowly to center dog over the opening without crossing wrists.
Avoid pushing right wrist farther into its yaw limit. Shift lifted basket slightly under the dog and move right forward to center above the opening.
Fine-center the dog within the basket walls by shifting basket slightly under it and right wrist inward a small amount; keep both grasps closed.
Dog is over the basket interior. Open only right jaws to release it, then withdraw slightly while left maintains the basket lift.
